slides.title: Pseudo‑Elements 🧬
slides.content:
# Style Specific Parts of an Element

Pseudo‑elements target a portion of an element that doesn't exist as a separate DOM node. They use double colons (`::`) to distinguish from pseudo‑classes.

Common pseudo‑elements:
- `::before` – insert content before the element's actual content.
- `::after` – insert content after.
- `::first-line` – the first formatted line.
- `::first-letter` – the first letter.
- `::selection` – the portion highlighted by the user.
- `::placeholder` – the placeholder text of an input.

slides.title: `::before` and `::after` 🎭

quizData.question: Without the `content` property, `::before` and `::after` will not render.
quizData.explanation: `content` is mandatory for these pseudo‑elements; they are invisible otherwise.

quizData.question: Which pseudo‑element styles the text a user has highlighted?
quizData.explanation: `::selection` applies styles to the portion of the document highlighted by the user.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## `::before` is Not in the DOM

Content generated by pseudo‑elements is not part of the actual document, so it won't be copied or read by some screen readers. Don't use it for critical information.
